paragraphs: Sanmina Corporation ("we" or "Sanmina" or the "Company") is a leading global provider of integrated manufacturing solutions, components, products and repair, logistics and after-market services. We provide these comprehensive offerings primarily to original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs") in the following industries: industrial, medical, defense and aerospace, automotive, communications networks and cloud infrastructure. Our customer-focused organization with 39,000 employees, including 4,000 temporary employees, supports our customers from 20 countries on four continents. We locate our facilities near our customers and their end markets in major centers for the electronics industry or in lower-cost locations. The combination of our advanced technologies, extensive manufacturing expertise and economies of scale enables us to meet the specialized needs of our customers. All references in this report to years refer to our fiscal years unless otherwise noted.
Our end-to-end solutions, combined with our global supply chain management expertise, allow us to manage our customers' products throughout their life cycles. These solutions include:
•product design and engineering, including concept development, detailed design, prototyping, validation, preproduction services and manufacturing design release and product industrialization;
•manufacturing of components, subassemblies and complete systems; •high-level assembly and test;
•direct order fulfillment and logistics services; •after-market product service and support; and
We manage our operations as two businesses:

1) Integrated Manufacturing Solutions ("IMS"). IMS is a single operating segment consisting of printed circuit board ("PCB") assembly and test, high-level assembly and test and direct order fulfillment. This segment generated approximately 80% of our total revenue in 2025.

2) Components, Products and Services ("CPS"). Components include advanced PCBs, backplanes and backplane assemblies, cable assemblies, fabricated metal parts, precision machined parts, and plastic injected molded parts. Products include optical, radio frequency ("RF") and microelectronic design and manufacturing services from our Advanced Microsystems Technologies division; multi-chip package memory solutions from our Viking Technology division; high-performance storage platforms for hyperscale and enterprise solutions from our Viking Enterprise Solutions division; defense and aerospace products, design, manufacturing, repair and refurbishment services from our SCI Technology, Inc. ("SCI") subsidiary; and cloud-based smart manufacturing execution software from our 42Q division. Services include design, engineering, logistics and repair and direct order fulfillment. CPS generated approximately 20% of our total revenue in 2025.

We target markets that we believe offer significant growth opportunities and in which OEMs sell complex mission critical products that are subject to strict regulatory requirements and/or rapid technological change. We believe these markets offer an opportunity to deliver higher margins as they require higher value-added manufacturing services and provide better opportunities for us to sell customers our advanced vertically integrated components. In addition, diversification across market segments and customers helps mitigate our dependency on any market or customer. We report our end markets as follows:
1) Industrial, Medical, Defense and Aerospace, and Automotive:

a. Industrial. Power generation, distribution, storage and controls for grid, data center, commercial and home applications. Industry 4.0 enabling, warehouse and factory asset management equipment, test and measurement systems and connected factory manufacturing software. Next generation semiconductor emulation and fabrication equipment supporting current and next generation artificial intelligence ("AI") solutions.

b. Medical. Disposable, wearable and consumable products supporting glucose sensing, insulin and drug delivery, cancer treatment and general health monitoring. Lab diagnostic, life sciences, lab processing
equipment, high volume automated labs, point of care and personal use devices. Next generation imaging, monitoring and therapeutic delivery systems.

c. Defense and Aerospace. Federal, regional, municipal and commercial surveillance systems, secure network communication systems and personal protection devices. Federal and commercial manned and unmanned aerospace products.

headings: Adverse changes in the key end markets we target could harm our business by reducing our sales.
Our operating results are subject to significant uncertainties, which can cause our future sales, net income and cash generated from operations to be variable.
We are subject to risks arising from our international operations.
We rely on a relatively small number of customers for a substantial portion of our sales and declines in sales to these customers could significantly reduce our net sales and net income.
Customer order cancellations, push-outs and reduced forecasts could reduce our sales, net income and liquidity.
Our strategy to pursue higher margin business depends in part on the success of our CPS businesses, which, if not successful, could cause our future gross margins and operating results to be lower.
Transfers of business or operations may increase our costs and cause disruptions in our ability to service our customers.
We are subject to a number of U.S. export control and regulatory requirements relating to our defense business, with which the failure to comply could result in fines and reduction of future revenue.

If we are unable to protect our intellectual property or if we infringe, or are alleged to infringe, upon the intellectual property of others, we could be required to pay significant amounts in costs or damages.
Allegations of failures to comply with domestic or international employment and related laws could result in the payment of significant damages, which would reduce our net income.
Cyberattacks and other disruptions of our information technology network and systems could interrupt our operations, lead to loss of our customer and employee data and subject us to damages.
Any failure to comply with applicable environmental laws could adversely affect our business by causing us to pay significant amounts for cleanup of hazardous materials or for damages or fines.
Global, national and corporate initiatives addressing climate change could increase our costs.
Our customers could experience credit problems, which could reduce our future revenue and net income.
We are subject to intense competition in the electronics manufacturing services ("EMS") industry, which could cause us to lose sales and, therefore, harm our financial performance.
Consolidation in the electronics industry may adversely affect our business by increasing customer buying power and increasing prices we pay for components.
We can experience losses due to foreign exchange rate fluctuations and currency controls, which could reduce our net income and impact our ability to repatriate funds.
We may not have sufficient insurance coverage for potential claims and losses, which could leave us responsible for certain costs and damages.
Recruiting and retaining our key personnel is critical to the continued growth of our business.
We are subject to risks associated with natural disasters and global events.
Risks of Investing in Our Stock
The market price of our common stock is volatile and is impacted by factors other than our financial performance.
paragraphs: We provide products and services to companies that serve the industrial, medical, defense and aerospace, automotive, communications networks and cloud infrastructure industries. Adverse changes in any of these end markets could reduce demand for our customers' products or make these customers more sensitive to the cost of our products and services, either of which could reduce our sales, gross margins and net income. A number of factors could affect these industries in general and our customers in particular, leading to reductions in net sales. These factors include:
•intense competition among our customers and their competitors, leading to reductions in prices for their products and increases in pricing pressure placed on us;
•failure of our customers' products to gain widespread commercial acceptance, which could decrease the volume of orders our customers place with us;
•changes in regulatory requirements affecting the products we build for our customers, leading to product redesigns or obsolescence and potentially causing us to lose business; and
•the negative effects of inflation, high interest rates and any potential resultant recession on customers' end markets and their demand for our products and services.

We realize a substantial portion of our revenue from communications equipment customers, including cloud service providers and data center operators. This market is highly competitive, particularly in the area of price. Should any of our larger customers in this market fail to effectively compete with their competitors, they could reduce their orders to us or experience liquidity difficulties, either of which could have the effect of substantially reducing our revenue and net income.

We are a leading global provider of integrated manufacturing solutions, components, products and repair, logistics and after-market services. Our revenue is generated from sales of our products and services primarily to original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs") that serve the industrial, medical, defense and aerospace, automotive, communications networks and cloud solutions industries.
Our operations are managed as two businesses:

1) Integrated Manufacturing Solutions ("IMS"). IMS is a single operating segment consisting of printed circuit board ("PCB") assembly and test, high-level assembly and test and direct-order-fulfillment.

2) Components, Products and Services ("CPS"). Components include advanced PCBs, backplanes and backplane assemblies, cable assemblies, fabricated metal parts, precision machined parts, and plastic injected molded parts. Products include optical, radio frequency ("RF") and microelectronic design and manufacturing services from our Advanced Microsystems Technologies division; multi-chip package memory solutions from our Viking Technology division; high-performance storage platforms for hyperscale and enterprise solutions from our Viking Enterprise Solutions division; defense and aerospace products, design, manufacturing, repair and refurbishment services from our SCI Technology, Inc. ("SCI") subsidiary; and cloud-based smart manufacturing execution software from our 42Q division. Services include design, engineering, and logistics and repair.

Our only reportable segment for financial reporting purposes is IMS, which represented approximately 80% of our total revenue in 2025. Our CPS business consists of multiple operating segments which do not individually meet the quantitative thresholds for being presented as reportable segments. Therefore, financial information for these operating segments is combined and presented in a single category called "CPS".

Our strategy is to leverage our comprehensive product and service offerings, advanced technologies and global capabilities to further penetrate diverse end markets that we believe offer significant growth opportunities and have complex products that require higher value-added services. We believe this strategy differentiates us from our competitors and will help drive more sustainable revenue growth and provide opportunities for us to achieve operating margins that exceed industry standards.

A core component of our business strategy is to secure and retain long-term customer partnerships with leading companies in growth industries, capitalizing on our global/regional footprint and unique value proposition in advanced electronics manufacturing. We provide tailored solutions by leveraging our technical capabilities in design, technology, assembly, integration, and after-sales services, aligning them with facilities globally. Historically, we have had substantial recurring sales to existing customers. Sales to our ten largest customers represent approximately 50% of net sales.

We typically enter into long-term supply agreements with our major OEM customers. These agreements generally have terms ranging from three to five years and cover the manufacture of a range of products. Under these agreements, we manufacture products to customers' unique specification leveraging our global factory footprint in locations chosen by our customers. However, these agreements generally do not obligate the customer to purchase minimum quantities of products. In addition, some customer contracts contain cost reduction objectives, which can have the effect of reducing revenue from such customers.

We generate about 80% of our net sales from products manufactured in our foreign operations. The concentration of foreign operations has resulted primarily from a desire on the part of many of our customers to manufacture in lower-cost locations in regions such as Latin America, Asia and Eastern Europe and we plan to expand our presence as appropriate to meet the needs of our customers. We also intend to continue to invest in factory automation, process improvements, robotics and artificial intelligence, keeping up with the trends in technology to further enhance our efficiency output.

We believe our end-to-end manufacturing solutions combined with our global supply chain management expertise differentiate us from our competitors and enable us to better serve the needs of OEM customers. However, our business faces many challenges. For example, we compete with a number of companies in each of our key end markets. This includes companies that are much larger than we are and smaller companies that focus on a particular niche product, service or end market. Although we believe we are well-positioned in each of our key end markets and offer many advantages compared to our competitors, profitably growing revenues are often constrained by intense competition. Additionally, we are impacted by macroeconomic challenges such as tariffs, inflation, supply chain constraints, foreign currency fluctuations, high interest rates, market volatility and recession concerns that have been and could be in the future exacerbated by geopolitical environment such as the tensions between the U.S. and other nations, conflict in the Middle East and the war in Ukraine.

Further, uncertainties around U.S. tariffs, retaliatory tariffs from other countries, and import/export restrictions may impact customer decisions to use our services in certain manufacturing locations and increase the complexity and cost of our supply chain. Although our customers are generally liable for tariffs we pay for components and finished products, our gross margins could be impacted if we are unable to fully recover these costs. The timing of tariff recovery from customers could adversely affect our operating cash flow in a given period.

Despite these challenges, we remain focused on improving our operations, building flexibility and efficiencies in our processes and adjusting our business models to changing circumstances. We intend to continue diversifying into mission critical markets and creating a portfolio of more complex, higher technology products with longer product life cycles. As our end markets evolve and grow, our ability to optimize our product and portfolio mix towards higher value opportunities will continue to be an important driver for our business going forward.

In line with our strategic intent to expand our presence in the Cloud and Artificial Intelligence ecosystem, we acquired the data center infrastructure manufacturing business, excluding certain research and development functions, of ZT Group Int'l, Inc. ("ZT Systems"), from AMD Design, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. On October 27, 2025 (the "Closing Date"), we completed the acquisition of ZT Systems (the "ZT Acquisition") for an aggregate consideration of $1.6 billion consisting of $1.46 billion in cash consideration (subject to adjustment for certain working capital and other items), a number of shares of our common stock valued at $150 million and up to $450 million contingent cash consideration upon the achievement of certain financial metrics during the three-year period following the closing of ZT Systems acquisition.

paragraphs: Sanmina Corporation ("we" or "Sanmina" or the "Company") 為全球領先的整合製造解決方案、零組件、產品與維修、物流及後市場服務供應商。我們主要為以下產業的原始設備製造商 ("OEMs") 提供這些全面的服務：工業、醫療、防禦與航太、汽車、通訊網路及雲端基礎建設。我們以客戶為中心的組織，擁有 39,000 名員工，包括 4,000 名臨時員工，支援來自四大洲 20 個國家的客戶。我們的設施位於電子產業主要中心或成本較低的地區，以靠近客戶及其最終市場。我們先進的技術、廣泛的製造專業知識與規模經濟的結合，使我們能夠滿足客戶的特殊需求。本報告中所有提及年份的參考皆指我們的會計年度，除非另有說明。
我們的端到端解決方案，結合全球供應鏈管理專業知識，使我們能夠管理客戶產品在其生命週期中的各階段。這些解決方案包括：
•產品設計與工程，包括概念開發、詳細設計、原型製作、驗證、預生產服務與製造設計發佈及產品產業化；
•零組件、子組裝件與完整系統的製造；•高階組裝與測試；
•直接訂單履行與物流服務；•後市場產品服務與支援；
我們將營運管理為兩大業務：
1) 整合製造解決方案 ("IMS")。IMS 為單一營運分部，包含印刷電路板 ("PCB") 組裝與測試、高階組裝與測試及直接訂單履行。此分部在 2025 年產生約 80% 的總營業收入。

2) 零組件、產品與服務 ("CPS")。零組件包括先進 PCB、背板與背板組裝、電纜組裝、金屬加工零件、精密機械加工零件及塑膠射出成型零件。產品包括來自我們 Advanced Microsystems Technologies 分部的光學、無線電頻率 ("RF") 及微電子設計與製造服務；來自我們 Viking Technology 分部的多晶片封裝記憶體解決方案；來自我們 Viking Enterprise Solutions 分部的高階儲存平台，用於超規模與企業解決方案；來自我們 SCI Technology, Inc. ("SCI") 子公司的防禦與航太產品、設計、製造、維修與翻新服務；以及來自我們 42Q 分部的雲端智慧製造執行軟體。服務包括設計、工程、物流與維修及直接訂單履行。CPS 在 2025 年產生約 20% 的總營業收入。
我們目標市場為我們認為具有顯著成長機會的市場，且在這些市場中，OEMs 售出複雜的關鍵任務產品，這些產品受到嚴格的法規要求和/或快速的技術變革所影響。我們認為這些市場提供機會，以提供更高的毛利率，因為這些市場需要更高價值的製造服務，並為我們提供更好的機會，向客戶銷售我們先進的垂直整合零組件。此外，跨市場區段和客戶的多元化有助於降低我們對任何市場或客戶的依賴。我們將終端市場報告如下：
1) 工業、醫療、防禦與航太，以及汽車：
a. 工業。電力發電、分配、儲存與控制，用於電網、資料中心、商業與住宅應用。產業 4.0 使能設備，倉庫與工廠資產管理設備，測試與量測系統，以及連網工廠製造軟體。支援現有及下一代人工智慧（"AI"）解決方案的下一代半導體模擬與製造設備。
b. 醫療。支援血糖感測、胰島素及藥物輸送、癌症治療及一般健康監測的消耗性、可穿戴式及一次性產品。實驗室診斷、生命科學、實驗室處理
設備、高產能自動化實驗室、即時診斷及個人使用裝置。下一代影像、監測及治療系統。
c. 防衛與航空太空。聯邦、區域、市級及商業監控系統、安全網路通訊系統及個人防護裝置。聯邦及商業有人及無人航空產品。

我們是全球領先的整合製造解決方案、零組件、產品及維修、物流及後市場服務供應商。我們的營業收入主要來自向原始設備製造商（"OEMs"）銷售產品與服務，這些OEMs服務於工業、醫療、防禦與航空航天、汽車、通訊網路及雲端解決方案產業。
我們的業務運作分為兩個業務部門：
1) 整合製造解決方案（"IMS"）。IMS為單一運作部門，包含印刷電路板（"PCB"）組裝與測試、高階組裝與測試及直接訂單履行。

2) 零組件、產品與服務（"CPS"）。零組件包括先進PCB、背板與背板組裝、電纜組裝、金屬加工零件、精密機械加工零件及塑膠射出成型零件。產品包括來自我們Advanced Microsystems Technologies部門的光學、無線電頻率（"RF"）及微電子設計與製造服務；來自我們Viking Technology部門的多晶片封裝記憶體解決方案；來自我們Viking Enterprise Solutions部門的高階儲存平台，用於超規模及企業解決方案；來自我們SCI Technology, Inc.（"SCI"）子公司防禦與航空航天產品、設計、製造、維修及翻新服務；以及來自我們42Q部門的雲端智慧製造執行軟體。服務包括設計、工程、物流及維修。
我們在財務報告目的上唯一的應報告部門為IMS，該部門在2025年約佔總營業收入的80%。我們的CPS業務包含多個運作部門，這些部門 individually 不符合被列為應報告部門的量化門檻。因此，這些運作部門的財務資訊被合併並以單一類別稱為"CPS"呈現。
我們的策略是利用我們全面的產品與服務組合、先進技術及全球能力，進一步深入我們認為有顯著成長機會且產品複雜、需要更高價值附加服務的多樣終端市場。我們相信此策略使我們與競爭對手有所區隔，並有助於推動更可持續的營收成長，並為我們創造營運毛利超過產業標準的機會。
我們業務策略的核心組成部分是與成長產業中的領先企業建立並維持長期客戶合作關係，利用我們的全球/區域足跡及在先進電子製造方面的獨特價值主張。我們透過善用在設計、技術、組裝、整合及後銷售服務方面的技術能力，提供量身打造的解決方案，並與全球設施對齊。歷來，我們對現有客戶有相當程度的持續銷售。我們前十大的客戶銷售佔總淨銷售額約50%。
我們通常會與主要的OEM客戶簽訂長期供應協議。這些協議的期限一般為三至五年，涵蓋多種產品的製造。根據這些協議，我們根據客戶的獨特規格製造產品，利用我們在全球各地廠區的設施，這些廠區的所在地由客戶選擇。然而，這些協議通常不會要求客戶購買最低數量的產品。此外，一些客戶契約包含成本降低目標，這可能會降低來自這些客戶的收入。
我們約80%的淨銷售額來自於我們海外廠區製造的產品。海外廠區的集中主要是因為許多客戶希望在拉丁美洲、亞洲和東歐等地區的低成本地點進行製造，我們計畫根據客戶需求適當擴大我們的業務佈局。我們也計畫持續投資於廠區自動化、製程改進、機械手臂與人工智慧，跟上科技趨勢以進一步提升我們的生產效率。

我們相信我們端到端的製造解決方案，加上我們全球供應鏈管理的專業知識，使我們與競爭對手有所區隔，並能更好地服務OEM客戶。然而，我們的業務面臨許多挑戰。例如，我們在每個關鍵終端市場都與多家公司競爭。這包括比我們規模更大的公司，以及專注於特定產品、服務或終端市場的較小公司。雖然我們認為我們在每個關鍵終端市場都有良好的定位，並相比競爭對手擁有許多優勢，但獲利性地增長收入往往受到激烈競爭的限制。此外，我們受到總體經濟挑戰的影響，例如關稅、通貨膨脹、供應鏈限制、外幣波動、高利率、市場波動以及經濟衰退的擔憂，這些問題過去和未來都可能因地緣政治環境如美國與其他國家的緊張關係、中東衝突以及烏克蘭戰爭而更加嚴重。
此外，美國關稅、其他國家的報復性關稅以及進出口限制的不確定性，可能影響客戶在某些製造地點使用我們服務的決定，並增加我們供應鏈的複雜性和成本。雖然我們的客戶通常需承擔我們支付的零組件和成品的關稅，但如果我們無法完全回收這些成本，我們的毛利率可能會受到影響。從客戶那裡回收關稅的時間點，可能會在特定期間內不利於我們的營運現金流。
儘管有這些挑戰，我們仍然專注於改善我們的業務運作，建立我們流程的靈活性與效率，並根據變化的環境調整我們的商業模式。我們計畫持續拓展至關鍵任務市場，並建立一個包含更多複雜、更高科技產品且產品生命週期更長的產品組合。當我們的終端市場持續演化與成長時，我們優化產品與組合結構以朝向更高價值機會的能力，將會是我們未來業務的重要驅動力。

依照本公司戰略意圖擴展在雲端與人工智慧生態系的佈局，我們取得 ZT Group Int'l, Inc.（"ZT Systems"）的資料中心基礎建設製造業務，排除部分研究與開發功能，自 AMD Design, LLC，為 Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. 的 wholly owned subsidiary 所擁有。於 2025 年 10 月 27 日（"交易日"），我們完成對 ZT Systems 的收購（"ZT 收購"），總計支付金額為 1.6 十億美元，包含 1.46 十億美元現金（視特定營運資金及其他項目進行調整），若干本公司普通股股份價值為 150 百萬美元，以及最高達 450 百萬美元的條件式現金支付，條件為在 ZT Systems 收購後三年期間達成特定財務指標。

headings: 我們所目標的關鍵終端市場出現不利變動，可能損害我們的業務，導致我們的銷售額減少。
我們的營運結果受到重大不確定性影響，這可能導致我們未來的銷售額、淨利潤及營運產生的現金流變動。
我們受到國際營運相關風險的影響。
我們依賴較少數的客戶來貢獻我們銷售額的很大一部分，這些客戶銷售額的減少可能顯著降低我們的淨銷售額與淨利潤。
客戶訂單取消、延後或預測減少，可能導致我們的銷售額、淨利潤與流動性下降。
我們追求高毛利業務的策略部分取決於我們的CPS業務成功，若這些業務未能成功，可能導致我們未來的毛利率與營運結果降低。
業務或營運的轉移可能增加我們的成本，並導致我們服務客戶的能力受到幹擾。
本公司受美國出口管制及相關規範的影響，與防禦業務相關，若未能遵守，可能導致罰款及未來收入減少。
若本公司無法保護智慧財產權，或若本公司侵權或被指控侵權，可能需支付大量成本或賠償金額。
若被指控未遵守國內或國際就業及相關法律，可能導致支付大量賠償金額，進而降低本公司淨收入。
網路攻擊及其他資訊科技網路與系統的中斷，可能影響本公司營運，導致客戶與員工資料遺失，並使本公司面臨賠償。
若未能遵守適用的環境法規，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響，導致需支付大量金額用以清理有害物質或賠償與罰款。
全球、國家及企業層面針對氣候變遷的措施，可能提高本公司成本。
本公司客戶可能遭遇信用問題，這可能會減少我們未來的營業收入與淨收入。
我們在電子製造服務（"EMS"）產業面臨激烈的競爭，這可能會導致我們失去銷售額，進而損害我們的財務表現。
電子產業的整併可能會對我們的業務產生負面影響，透過增加客戶的採購權力以及我們為零組件所支付的價格。
我們可能因外匯匯率波動及貨幣管制而遭受損失，這可能會減少我們的淨收入，並影響我們將資金匯回的能力。
我們可能無法為潛在的索賠與損失提供足夠的保險保障，這可能會使我們需承擔某些成本與損害。
招募與留住我們的關鍵人才對我們業務的持續成長至關重要。
我們面臨與天然災害及全球事件相關之風險。
投資本公司股票之風險
本公司普通股之市場價格波動性高，且受除本公司財務表現之外之因素影響。
paragraphs: 本公司提供產品與服務予服務於工業、醫療、防禦與航太、汽車、通訊網路及雲端基礎建設產業的公司。這些終端市場若發生不利變動，可能會降低客戶產品的需求，或使這些客戶對本公司產品與服務的價格更加敏感，進而降低本公司的銷售額、毛利率與淨收入。這些產業整體以及本公司客戶可能受到多種因素影響，導致淨銷售額減少。這些因素包括：
• 本公司客戶及其競爭對手之間的激烈競爭，導致其產品價格下降，並增加對本公司產品與服務的價格壓力；
• 本公司客戶產品未能獲得廣泛商業接受度，可能會降低客戶向本公司下訂單的數量；
• 影響本公司為客戶製造產品的規範變動，導致產品重新設計或過時，並可能導致本公司失去業務；以及
• 通貨膨脹、高利率及任何可能引發的經濟衰退對客戶終端市場及其對本公司產品與服務需求的負面影響。
本公司來自通訊設備客戶的收入佔相當大比例，包括雲端服務供應商與資料中心營運商。此市場競爭激烈，尤其在價格方面。若此市場中任何主要客戶無法有效與其競爭對手競爭，可能會減少其向本公司下訂單，或遭遇流動性困難，進而大幅降低本公司的收入與淨收入。
